episodes.200097: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the morning and into the afternoon ahead of an approaching warm front on Monday (4/28).  Storms during the morning and afternoon mainly produced hail up to quarter size. Additional showers and thunderstorms developed during the evening ahead of an approaching cold front on Monday (4/28).  The storms during the evening produced large hail up to quarter size, damaging winds, and tornadoes.
episodes.200107: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northeast Nebraska during the evening. One storm reached severe strength as it tracked through Knox and Cedar Counties, producing hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter. Additionally, measured wind gusts of 59 and 63 mph were reported near Neligh, NE���likely associated with the evaporation of anvil precipitation, which helped mix down strong winds from the low-level jet.
episodes.200270: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms impacted a large portion of the western Nebraska Panhandle during the evening hours on 4/27, with the strongest storms impacting primarily Dawes and Box Butte counties. These storms produced gusty winds and hail.
episodes.200328: A system that brought isolated thunderstorms to the region late on April 27th into the early morning hours of April 28th generated half dollar sized hail near the Pierre Regional Airport and a peak wind gust of 69 mph at the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 2 miles west of Oacoma.
episodes.200566: Strong to severe thunderstorms had developed across a surface cold front that moved east across Minnesota during the afternoon hours of April 28th. Increased southerly moisture transport from a +50kt low-level jet had reached as far north as the Twin Cities metro which helped destabilize the environment. A few supercells were able to develop and produce hail mainly quarter size to ping-pong ball size although the largest hail stone was golf ball size six miles south of Owatonna.  ||This line of storms also produced two tornadoes in Rice and Goodhue Counties which causing heavy damage to several semi-and tanker trucks, collapsing building walls and a few farm outbuildings. Maximum estimated tornadic wind speeds were 110 mph.
episodes.200641: Although large scale lift was weak on the afternoon and evening of the 27th, severe thunderstorms were still able to develop across the central South Plains. A dryline was again in place cutting from north to south around the Interstate 27/US Highway 87 corridor creating low level convergence. Strong heating along the dryline allowed a capping inversion to break late in the afternoon. With ample moisture in place at the lowest levels of the atmosphere, isolated storms were able to take advantage of a very unstable atmosphere. Isolated thunderstorms initially developed in and around the Lubbock (Lubbock County) vicinity and moved northeastward producing severe wind gusts along with hail up to ping pong ball size.
episodes.200690: A cold front moving through the area brought showers and thunderstorms, a few of which were severe with large hail and damaging wind. The area around Brookfield in Tift county saw particularly significant wind damage.
episodes.200709: In the late afternoon to evening hours, scattered storms developed and trained across portions of northeast Kansas, leading to isolated reports of Flash Flooding with up to 5 inches of rainfall reported. These storms also produced hail to baseball size, wind gusts to 70 mph, and a brief tornado in Pottawatomie county.
episodes.200769: An approaching upper-level disturbance would cause brief high winds and light showers along a dryline across the Permian Basin and Trans Pecos. Ahead of the dryline, severe thunderstorms impacted eastern portions of the Permian Basin.
episodes.200835: Isolated non-severe thunderstorms moved across the region on the morning of the 28th. One of the storms produced a bolt of lightning in the Lincoln Park area of Duluth that hit a parked truck. The truck then started on fire sustaining heavy damage.
episodes.201017: Heavy rainfall across Pohnpei brought 3 to 5 inches across the island with most of the rain falling over a 4 to 5 hour period.
episodes.201376: Severe storms developed across western South Dakota and brought severe hail and wind.
episodes.201378: Overnight severe weather produces a tornado in Rosebud.
episodes.201550: A longwave trough across the western US moved east with a resulting surface low deepening across the central plains and lifting into Iowa. Lapse rates steepened through the day and MLCAPE values surged past 3000 J/kg, accompanied by deep layer shear around 40-50 kts. Even so, uncertainty existed at the time regarding how widespread storm coverage would be given a stout cap in place. Hodographs indicated SRH of up to 300 m2/s2, supporting rotating storms with a conditional tornadic threat should that cap be overcome. At the end of the day the full environmental potential was not realized and no tornadoes were reported, however a number of storms produced large hail and damaging winds. Storms initialized in northwest Iowa in the afternoon along the dryline, and moving across northern Iowa through the evening. These storms produced quarter up to golf ball sized hail. A second area of thunderstorms developed across central Iowa in the evening, fueled by a strengthening low level jet.  Additionally, light showers lifted out of Missouri and into southern Iowa by late evening. Despite no lightning in the area and very light to no precipitation occurring at the time of reports, multiple sites in southern Iowa reported gusts over 60 mph along with one report of damage to a barn.
episodes.201604: An upper level trough of low pressure aloft was situated over the Intermountain West on April 27th. East of this feature, a warm front lifted into western Nebraska and became the focal point for thunderstorm development during the late afternoon hours. Initial thunderstorms developed over western Garden County and tracked northeast into abundant low level moisture, strong low level shear and increased instability where they quickly became severe.  Hail up to 3 inches in diameter and eleven tornadoes occurred  with the severe storms which continued into the mid evening hours. Activity finally weakened over northern Cherry County by late evening. A couple of tornadoes were rated EF2 with winds estimated up to 132 MPH.
episodes.201684: Broad southwesterly upper-tropospheric flow comprised the south-central CONUS on the 28th. An embedded system instigated scattered thunderstorm development across the Red River Valley during the evening into overnight hours. With strong instability and sufficient wind shear in place, a mix of supercell and clustered storm modes occurred during this time, producing large to very large hail.
episodes.201685: Broad southwesterly upper-tropospheric flow comprised the south-central CONUS on the 28th. An embedded system instigated scattered thunderstorm development across the Red River Valley during the evening into overnight hours. With strong instability and sufficient wind shear in place, a mix of supercell and clustered storm modes occurred during this time, producing large to very large hail and occasional thunderstorm wind damage.
episodes.201693: A line of thunderstorms, developed from around Ogallala to Spencer Nebraska, during the mid afternoon hours of April 28th. As this activity tracked east, the northern portion of the line produced hail up to quarter size in Holt County.
episodes.201698: A spring system that produced snow in the mountains brought early season storms to the lower elevations.
episodes.201785: The combination of abundant low level moisture and strong instability produced a few severe thunderstorms. The severe storms produced large hail.
episodes.201821: A line of severe storms moved through portions of southeast Minnesota during the evening on April 28th and produced scattered instances of up to quarter sized hail.
episodes.201866: A low pressure lifting through the region on the 28th resulted in strong thunderstorms that produced severe hail, strong winds, and flooding rainfall.
episodes.201957: A storm developed then intensified over eastern Saline County during the late afternoon into the early evening of the 28th. The storm tracked northeast and produced two inch hail near New Cambria.
episodes.202108: Two rounds of severe storms moved through portions of west-central Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours. The first round resulted in an isolated storm in Clark County that produced hail up to half dollar sized. A second round progressed through the area which produced a brief tornado northeast of Mondovi, Wisconsin and an isolated wind gust to 60 mph in Clark County.
episodes.202136: From April 26 through 30, a moist and unstable weather pattern affected Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The episode began as deep tropical moisture moved into the region from the southeast, interacting with deep-layer troughs and supportive jet dynamics aloft. This synoptic setup led to daily rounds of scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms, especially during the afternoons across the interior and western portions of Puerto Rico.
episodes.202163: A line of thunderstorms developed on the nose of a low-level jet, just in advance of a cold front across the central Dakotas. Deep-layer shear of 30-40 knots was largely parallel to the boundary and storms rapidly became linear with spotty damaging wind.
episodes.202179: Thunderstorms erupted along a cold front and a post-frontal boundary during the afternoon and early evening of April 28. Steep mid-level lapse rates around 8C/km and 55 to 65 knots of deep-layer shear led to severe storm structures, which evolved toward smaller-scale linear features along strong outflow pools with 60 to 65 mph winds during the event. Post-frontal storms developed in an environment of up to 1000 J/kg MUCAPE which favored mainly large hail.
episodes.202181: Thunderstorms erupted along a cold front and a post-frontal boundary during the afternoon and early evening of April 28.
